slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Many clients, one estate, and confidentiality between them

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Firms that work inside other people’s businesses carry a particular obligation: information from one client must not become visible to another, even accidentally, and even when the same consultant works on both. That is a structural requirement rather than a policy statement.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Separation by design, not by good intentions

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Per-client workspaces, permissions that expire when an engagement ends, and a clear rule for where client material is allowed to live. The alternative, a shared drive that nobody prunes, is where confidentiality quietly breaks down.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Working on the client’s site and the client’s network

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Consultants routinely connect to guest wireless, use client systems and move between environments in a week. Devices need to be secure enough to be trusted anywhere, which puts the emphasis on the endpoint and on identity rather than on the office perimeter.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Projects start and stop, so the setup has to as well

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Onboarding and offboarding are constant rather than occasional, and each one is an access decision. Automating joiners and leavers is the difference between a licence bill that reflects reality and one that only grows.
